representative_observations.reviewer: Codex same-Agent visual/AV review, with external KIE actual-audio perception; not independent human/native-speaker or company acceptance
representative_observations.method: Actual encoded frame crops and contact sheet inspected per occurrence; native copy, required original-letter removal, font shaping, moving phone UI and foreground clipping checked. All caption pixels decoded for timing. External model reviewed actual decoded audio, whose exact PCM identity is retained across visual-only revisions. Self-review is labeled; technical gates do not establish business acceptance.
representative_observations.lesson: Source-only repair was reused across eight languages. A bright foreground-hand mask must exclude dim thumbnail-photo skin; a generic rectangle or connected skin patch leaves source letters or clips native letters. Phone UI text must remain below the source-style caption capsule. Inspect the first source capsule/letter by frame index, not only the intended source caption interval. Actual spoken copy and caption are one script; final timing comes from adjusted voice and actual encoded pixels. These are observations on this one source, not cross-source proof.
limitations: Same-Agent visual and AV judgment plus independent provider audio-only analysis; no human/native-speaker or company acceptance.
Traditional local lettering repair with source-only neutral plates; local softness remains around repaired title areas, reflected in visual-fidelity score.
Original music and effects are retained, with local separated accompaniment during narration and modest ducking. Separation is not lossless.
No lip-sync model used. Creator handle, numeric counts/durations and handwritten palm initials are intentionally preserved.
The one authorized extra local correction contained failed partial implementations; those attempts and their evidence are retained, with no additional paid submission.

representative_observations.reviewer: Codex same-Agent review with attributed external audio-model perception; no independent whole-video or business approval
representative_observations.method: Inspected all eight localized caption/CTA instances in actual candidate galleries, original source timeline crops, full-frame candidate evidence and caption boundary frames. Reviewed decoded glyph timing, actual candidate WAV identity and source/candidate external audio comparisons. Findings include visual failures; scores never override them.
representative_observations.lesson: Same-source six-language preparation can share source analysis and background separation, but any visual repair defect propagates to every language. Source-local classical inpainting produced obvious patches; local LaMa improved text removal but left soft clothing/hair, apple/hand ghosting and source-colour/glyph fragments at transitions. These candidate videos remain revise. Exact native script, actual mixed-audio DTW, independent transcription, decoded glyph boundary measurements and mux timebase correlation are separate evidence. An invalid optional accent was rejected at createTask; singleton JSON review envelopes were recovered locally from saved receipts without another charge. One source and six locales are not six independent source validations.
limitations: Source-burned captions overlap moving clothing, hair, apple and fingers. Repairs create visible soft regions/ghost edges and occasional source-colour/glyph fragments around text transitions.
Uniform green native subtitles simplify the original per-word green/red/white highlight animation.
Native female dubbed audio retains original English mouth movements; no lip synchronization was performed.
Audio preservation is supported by local source separation, original post-7.8s samples, and external model perception; lossless separation is not claimed.
Same-Agent review plus external audio model and pixel/ASR measurements is not independent native-speaker, company or business acceptance.
